title: Microtrace Forensics — UX Scenarios & Sketches (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a set of small, distinct UX scenarios and quick sketches for a token-level / microtrace forensics view in the Console. Goal is to un-block engineering and design pairing for an initial MVP prototype that surfaces per-invocation cost and latency signals and supports fast root-cause of outliers (high-cost, high-latency).

Context and motivation:
- Customers repeatedly ask: why did this single invocation cost 45x our average?
- Current console aggregates hide the per-token effects of long system prompts, model n-gram bloats, or repeated tool calls.
- We need a targeted investigative flow (not a replacement for the holistic token explorer) that helps engineers and SREs triage and reduce unit-cost regressions quickly.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (SRE) doing incident triage: wants fast filtering by tail latency and token-cost anomalies.
- ML engineer or model owner debugging quality vs cost regressions: wants to inspect KV-cache reuse, quantized model fallbacks, and prompt expansion.
- Product engineer (customer) doing ad-hoc queries: wants an easy way to flag and annotate suspicious invocations.

High-level UX principles:
1) Low time-to-insight: 3 clicks from invocation list -> relevant token view.
2) Progressive disclosure: summary first, deep trace second (don’t overwhelm).
3) Actionable decisions: highlight cheapest mitigation levers (trim prompt, enable prefix caching, switch model variant).
4) Auditability: support notes, tags, and export for postmortems.

Scenario sketches (flows) — numbered for backlog refs:
1) "Fast Triage" (SRE)
   - Entry: Alerts page -> invocation list (sorted by tail latency)
   - Click on invocation row -> small details panel slides from right
   - Panel shows: overall latency, total tokens (in/out), token-cost breakdown sparkline, top-3 contributing spans (model decode, tool call, IO)
   - CTA: "Open microtrace" (full-screen modal)
   - Modal defaults to condensed waterfall with per-token bars color-coded by op type (model, tool, preproc). Hover shows token text, token-size, per-token time, and per-token cost estimate.
   - Quick actions in modal header: Annotate, Mark as false-positive, Create Jira.

2) "Quality vs Cost Investigator" (ML eng)
   - Entry: Model dashboard -> filter invocations by model version + date range
   - Use histogram of per-invocation avg token cost vs completion length -> select dense outlier bucket
   - Open an invocation -> show side-by-side: token waterfall + decoded text + KV cache hit overlay (green stripes where cache hit)
   - Enable toggles: show quantization fallback regions; show substitution score (diff from baseline model)

3) "Customer Quick Flag" (Product eng)
   - From a customer’s route details page, user selects an invocation and clicks "Flag for review" -> adds to shared investigation list with an optional comment
   - Lightweight view only (no heavy traces) with summary card and link to full modal for SREs

Wireframe descriptions (UI skeleton notes):
- Header: breadcrumb "Console > Invocations > Microtrace"
- Left rail: invocation list (search + date picker + filters: status, route, model, cost percentile)
- Primary canvas: invocation detail card + waterfall canvas (SVG-based; horizontal time axis; vertical token index)
- Waterfall legend: model decode (purple), tool/external (orange), preproc/tokenize (blue), KV cache hit (green hatch), blocked-wait (grey)
- Right rail (context): metadata (request id, user, route, model v, region), cost-breakdown pie (service, model, network), mitigations list (auto-suggested)
- Footer actions: annotate, export trace (.har-like), create incident, revert route-level config (if user has perms)

Interaction micro-patterns (edge cases):
- Very long invocations (>4096 tokens): auto-collapse after 500 tokens, offer "expand" with a heatmap overview to jump to segments
- Missing token text (redacted data): show token index + type + "(redacted)"; prevent copy; include link to KMS audit log
- Aggregation across models: when a single invocation triggered fallbacks, show layered timeline with toggle to isolate model variant timing

Metrics to validate UX choices:
- Time to first insight: measure time from invocation list click -> first token hover (target < 6s for modal open + render)
- Investigator retention: % of flagged invocations that get annotated or converted to ticket within 48h (target > 60%)
- Export rate: how often users export traces (helps justify export feature)

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Should per-token cost be estimated on-device (approx) or only returned by backend to ensure authoritative billing numbers? (lean backend-authoritative for simplicity, but prototype can show approximate estimates client-side)
- How much text should be shown inline vs via flyout for PII-sensitive tokens? (default redaction for tokens from request.body; explicit "show" with audit log required)
- Performance: can we stream waterfall tiles progressively to reduce TTFB for huge traces? (proto: implement incremental canvas rendering)

Backlog (scoped for 6-week sprint) — rough priorities:
- P1: Basic modal with invocation metadata, simple waterfall, hover tooltips (JIRA: INF-889)
- P1: Left-rail filtering and date picker + server-side query for top-1% cost invocations (INF-890)
- P2: KV cache overlay + quantization-fallback markers (INF-894)
- P2: Annotate + shared investigation list (INF-897)
- P3: Export trace / .har-like artifact (INF-900)
- P3: Progressive rendering for traces > 2k tokens (INF-902)
- Nice-to-have: In-modal suggested mitigations (trim prompt, enable prefix cache) with cost-savings estimate (research task)

Acceptance criteria (for P1):
- Modal opens and renders waterfall for invocations up to 1k tokens within 6s on medium test dataset
- Hovering a token shows token text (redacted per privacy rules), per-token latency, and cost estimate
- Left-rail filters can return top 100 invocations in <4s for 30-day window
- Basic annotation persists and appears in shared list for collaborators

Implementation notes for eng pairing:
- Backend: new endpoint /invocations/{id}/microtrace returns compressed trace objects (token-level times, op-type, token-text (nullable), cache_hit boolean) and per-token cost micro-estimates. Ensure endpoint supports range requests for progressive fetch.
- Frontend: SVG canvas + virtualized rows (do not render all tokens at once). Consider WebGL prototype if SVG becomes a bottleneck.
- Security: redact tokens unless user has "trace:unredact" role; log unredacts to audit stream.

Design TODOs for next sync with design (Wed 11am):
- Asha: produce 3 Figma frames: compact list -> modal collapsed -> modal expanded with KV overlay (due Mon)
- Diego: prototype incremental canvas renderer and share perf numbers (due Tue)
- Claire: draft API contract for microtrace endpoint + sample payload (PR to infra by EOD Fri)

Notes to self (rough):
- Think about a lightweight "heatmap scrubber" above waterfall to show where time is concentrated (users love summary visuals)
- Consider linking mitigation suggestions to Redwood Optimize hints so users can jump from triage -> auto-tuning
- Keep scope tight for first release; ship value to SREs quickly and iterate from feedback

References and inspiration:
- Figma frames: FIGMA-1234#frame-7 (proto sketches)
- Existing console invocations list: console/invocations-v2
- Customer ask: support thread in #cs-bugs from 2024-11-20 (Slack link above)
